title: POC: Harness script resilience & SLA matrix scoping
summary: Discovery + POC scoping to align on benchmark harness integration, resilience tests, SLA matrix and timeline. Customer wants to validate streaming vs non-streaming throughput, tail-latency under real scripts, and script-level retry behavior. Agreement to share sample harness adapter, provide tokenized script samples, and run a two-week pilot focused on p95/p99 tail behavior.
action_items: Marcus: send benchmark blueprint + sample harness adapter repo link by 2027-02-10
Rafael: share representative customer scripts (anonymized) and tokenization notes by 2027-02-11
Priya: draft SLA matrix with p50/p95/p99 targets and fallback policy by 2027-02-12
Maya: provide current infra topology and peak RPS numbers by 2027-02-12
Anya: confirm pilot stakeholders and legal/compliance contact for SOC2 docs by 2027-02-14
next_steps: Redwood to run small smoke run of harness with 100 RPS synthetic vs recorded script sample
Schedule 90-min technical deep-dive next week to walk through adapter mapping and replay
Customer to sign PO for 2-week pilot after review of blueprint and pricing sheet
meeting_header: Date: 2027-02-07 | Time: 15:00 PST | Duration: 1h08m | Location: Zoom
transcript:
[00:00] Marcus Li: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. I'm Marcus from Redwood, with Priya on the line — SE who will run the harness integration. Quick intros?
[00:12] Anya Petrov: Hi, Anya here, CTO at BrightCart. Rafael and Maya with me. We're trying to scope a POC to validate your inference runtime for checkout personalization at peak.
[00:22] Priya Nambiar: Nice to meet you all. Quick agenda: workload sizing, streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs, how customer scripts map into our harness, success criteria, and timeline.
[00:34] Rafael Gomez: Appreciate it. Short context — we're doing real-time product ranking during checkout. Typical session is 6 requests/user, avg 120 tokens per request, but some requests are up to 800 tokens when we include full history. Peak is ~2k RPS global across shard, regional peaks hit about 700 RPS.
[00:50] Maya Singh: And our SRE concerns are tail-latency and cold starts; we can't exceed 250ms p95 for the interactive path.
[01:02] Marcus Li: Okay that's helpful. Couple of quick clarifications: when you say 120 tokens avg — that's post-tokenization? Any custom tokenizers?
[01:12] Rafael Gomez: It's based on our text preproc, roughly aligned with GPT tokenization but there are small differences, we can export the tokenization mapping.
[01:20] Priya Nambiar: Great — bring the tokenized samples. It matters because batching and KV cache sizes change per token. Also note our runtime's batching rules and continuous batching will behave differently if the payload distribution is heavy-tailed.
[01:35] Anya Petrov: Streaming — we prefer streaming because UI shows progressive results, but if it kills tail-latency we might fallback to non-streaming. We want both tested.
[01:46] Marcus Li: Absolutely — pilot should include both modes. For streaming we measure first-byte latency and end-to-end completion. For non-streaming we measure overall request latency and throughput. We usually benchmark with three scripts: synthetic uniform, recorded replay, and worst-case long-history.
[02:02] Rafael Gomez: How do you handle KV cache penetration for recorded replays? Our sessions are often multi-turn with mostly overlap, so KV hit-rate matters.
[02:12] Priya Nambiar: We simulate KV reuse in the harness via session affinity — but worth instrumenting with your real traces. Sometimes the transcription in our past calls wrote KV 'cash' — small mis-typo — but we mean KV cache.
[02:25] Maya Singh: (laughs) heard that. Ok, on success criteria: we want p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms, p99 < 450ms on non-streaming for the happy path. Streaming target: first chunk p95 < 150ms. Cost target is equally important — want cost per 1k requests under our internal threshold.
[02:45] Marcus Li: We'll draft SLA matrix. Typical Redwood approach is we define SLO buckets: interactive, batch, and fallback. We'll propose canary policies — if p95 exceeds threshold for 5 min, route to smaller model or dedicated capacity.
[03:00] Rafael Gomez: Smaller model fallback is OK if quality delta is acceptable. We'll include quality checks (rerank evaluation) in acceptance criteria.
[03:10] Priya Nambiar: For the harness integration, we'll provide a small adapter that maps your script format to the harness. Two options: run the harness in streaming mode (client receives token deltas) or run as non-streaming but stream client-side updates. There's additional complexity with reconnects and resumed KV caches.
[03:30] Rafael Gomez: For reconnects we can't lose session context. Can you checkpoint KV cache across reconnects?
[03:36] Priya Nambiar: We can persist session context to optional external Redis during the pilot, but in private deployments you can choose on-disk or KMS-protected state. We'll show a few patterns in the deep-dive.
[03:49] Anya Petrov: Security: we need to review SOC2, KMS integration, and audit logs. Also want to confirm RBAC for who can trigger canaries.
[03:58] Marcus Li: We'll attach SOC2 + security whitepaper link in the follow-up. RBAC is supported via SSO/SAML and we can gate canary triggers.
[04:08] Maya Singh: Great. On data residency — some EU traffic must stay in-region. Can we pin routing?
[04:14] Marcus Li: Yes, routing policies can pin by region and by customer tier. For the pilot we can run in your preferred cloud region.
[04:22] Priya Nambiar: Back to harness specifics: Rafael, what format are your scripts — JSON lines, protobuf, or custom?
[04:29] Rafael Gomez: We have a custom JSON array that includes session id, turn history, user metadata. We'll produce an anonymized sample.
[04:36] Priya Nambiar: Perfect. Our adapter will accept that and we can provide a small mapping script. Also we'll need the tokenization output to avoid mismatched batch sizes.
[04:45] Marcus Li: Timeline proposal: Week 0 (this week) — exchange scripts and blueprint. Week 1 — integrate adapter and run smoke tests (100 RPS synthetic + recorded replay at low scale). Week 2 — scale to peak-ish load (700 RPS regional slices) and run long-run resilience tests including noise injection (network jitter, instance preempt). End of week 2 — review and acceptance. Does that timeline sound feasible?
[05:10] Anya Petrov: Yes, tight but doable. We need pricing to sign off — send a pilot quote tied to reserved infra or usage.
[05:18] Marcus Li: We'll include two pricing models: short-term reserved for predictability and pure usage. We'll highlight unit economics and per-token cost under quantized model profiles.
[05:28] Rafael Gomez: Quantized profiles — do you have 8-bit and 4-bit recommendations? We care about quality drop.
[05:34] Priya Nambiar: We'll surface model/quantization suggestions per workload. For long-history requests sometimes 4-bit introduces hallucination risks; we'll propose A/B with quality evals.
[05:44] Maya Singh: On telemetry: we need distributed tracing and per-token cost visibility. Can your console show per-route cost and p95 breakdown?
[05:52] Marcus Li: Yes, Redwood Console shows per-route token breakdown and latency histograms. We'll provide dashboard links for the pilot.
[05:59] Rafael Gomez: Are we doing mirrored traffic for real-world validation? We prefer mirror the live traffic to the pilot cluster for 24 hours before running load test.
[06:08] Priya Nambiar: Mirror is supported; we recommend a read-only mirror with rate-limited sampling to avoid doubled downstream effects. We'll coordinate on safe playback windows.
[06:18] Anya Petrov: A few curveballs: we sometimes have bursty events (promo launches) where RPS spikes 5-10x for short periods. We want to test burst absorption and autoscale behavior.
[06:30] Marcus Li: We'll include burst scenarios in the kit — step-ramp up to 10x over a 2-minute window and observe scaling. For Dedicated capacity we can define burst pools.
[06:40] Maya Singh: For logging and audit — need immutable logs for compliance, with retention policy.
[06:45] Marcus Li: That's part of the Private deployment package; for hosted we can offer extended retention as an add-on.
[06:52] Rafael Gomez: Good. Regarding failure modes: how do you handle partial streaming failures — like token stream cut mid-response?
[06:58] Priya Nambiar: Handler patterns: reconnect with resume token if possible; otherwise mark as failed and optionally replay last N tokens to rehydrate. We'll test those in harness.
[07:08] Anya Petrov: Ok, final recap?
[07:11] Marcus Li: Recap: Redwood to send blueprint, sample adapter repo, SOC2/security docs, pricing options. BrightCart to send anonymized scripts, tokenization output, infra topology, and compliance contact. Pilot timeline ~2 weeks with streaming and non-streaming benchmarks including burst tests, mirror run, and tail-latency analysis.
[07:32] Anya Petrov: Sounds right. Rafael will send the scripts. Maya will coordinate SRE sign-off.
[07:38] Marcus Li: Great — we'll follow up with calendar invite for the deep-dive and attach the blueprint. Thanks everyone.
[07:44] Priya Nambiar: Thanks all.
[07:46] (call ends)
